Draw a rectangle spanning x ~7%-93%, y ~36%-88% with no fill and a thin (~1.5pt) #C00000 outline. 4. Inside its upper-left, add a bullet list starting x ~12%, y ~40%: level-1 items (hollow-circle bullet markers colored #E1A760, text #3F3F3F ~20pt): 'Images are 2-D' and 'What does a 2-D input really mean?'; under the first add level-2 sub-bullets (~16pt, indented): 'k-D if you also count the extra channels' and 'RGB, hyperspectral, etc.'; under the second add 'Neighboring variables are locally correlated'. 5. Insert the Grumpy Cat meme image at top-right inside the frame (x ~66%-90%, y ~37%-60%); overlay white bold all-caps text 'I LOVE MATH' at its top and 'IT MAKES PEOPLE CRY!' at its bottom; draw a small no-fill rectangle with #FF0000 outline around the cat's nose/mouth. 6. Make three recolored duplicates of that meme (PowerPoint Picture Format > Color > recolor to red #B00000, green #00A000, blue #0000B0) and stack them at bottom-right (x ~63%-92%, y ~60%-87%) with offsets: red back-right, green middle, blue front-left, keeping captions visible on each. 7. Insert the zoomed, slightly rotated cat close-up photo at bottom-left (x ~28%-42%, y ~70%-86%). 8. Draw four thin block/line arrows pointing into the photo: orange #E8A020 from upper-left, yellow #F0E040 from the right, cyan #40C0D0 from the left, red #E02020 from lower-left. 9. Optionally add a small white arrow shape on the green channel image to mimic the captured cursor. 10. Do not add slide numbers, footers, or logos — none appear on the slide.
